posts.text:
Jensen Huang nearly lost NVIDIA three times before anyone cared.

First chip (NV1) bet on the wrong graphics math. Microsoft standardized on triangles. Almost everything shipped came back. Cash was measured in weeks.

He flew to Sega, admitted their next chip was a dead end, and asked them to cancel the contract but still pay the remaining money. They did. That cash bought one more shot.

RIVA 128 was designed almost entirely in simulation. No money for respins. It worked. A million units in four months. Company survived.

Years later, Intel used a licensing dispute to push NVIDIA out of the chipset business entirely. Jensen took the hit, exited, and doubled down elsewhere.

He then spent a decade building CUDA so GPUs could do more than graphics, for a market that barely existed. Wall Street hated it. He kept going.

When AI arrived, the architecture and software he had forced through were already there. One man absorbed the near-death cycles, the public failures, and the long years of no payoff, then delivered the platform the world is now running on.

That level of resilience, pain tolerance, and vision is rare. He should keep running NVIDIA.

posts.text:
Go-Ahead Make my day, prove Christianity is true with evidence  As I Prove here Truth of Islam.

Any claim without evidence is just a conjecture!
My argument is grounded in two unequivocal premises:

1. Anything that possesses a history must have a beginning and requires a source for its existence.

2. A deterministic system necessitates a designer.

Any entity that exhibits a change of state inherently has a history. 
History, by its nature, demands a beginning, as the concept of infinite history is illogical, irrational, and fundamentally impossible.

Consider the example of apples arranged on a table. When I place an apple down, then another, and another, a line of apples is formed. 
This line has an undeniable history: 

The second apple exists because of the first, and the third exists because of the second. If we have an existing line of apples, it cannot extend infinitely backward; an infinite line would imply the absence of a starting point. 
The recognition of a first apple instantly dispels the notion of infinity.

Thus, if we refer to apple X in a sequence, apple X-1 must precede it. The third apple cannot exist without the second, and the second without the first. 

The first apple cannot exist unless there are no apples at all. 
Therefore, the existence of this line of apples mandates a beginning. 
This reasoning applies universally to anything that exists and has a history.

Now, turning to our universe, scientific evidence confirms it had a beginning. 
Logically, this means that because our universe has a history, it requires a source for its existence.

This source cannot itself have a history; otherwise, we encounter the trap of infinite regression yet again. Consequently, this source must be, truly infinite ie. lacking both a beginning and an end.

Moreover, this source must possess the ability to create our universe spontaneously. If this source were part of our universe's history, it would be finite and would necessitate another source for its own existence.

Given that our universe contains information and we, as humans, possess the knowledge and the capacity for logical thought, all of this must arise from the source. 
The source must embody essential attributes and cannot include any that contradict these fundamental qualities.

Now, let's confront the second premise decisively. A deterministic system cannot arise from randomness, as randomness and determinism are fundamentally incompatible. 

There is no such thing as true randomness or "by chance." 

Instead, we experience bounded uncertainty. 
For example, no matter how many times a die is thrown, you will never roll a 7. The outcomes are limited to numbers between 1 and 6. When you plant an apple seed, there will not be a random emergence of an orange tree—unless external manipulation is involved.

Even at the quantum level, uncertainty remains bounded. Scientists assert that the Higgs boson is responsible for imparting mass and properties to all matter in our universe. If true randomness were a reality, 
we would observe various forms of matter emerging haphazardly, leading to chaos and ultimately the collapse of our universe. 
Stephen Hawking himself has warned that the so-called "God particle" (Higgs boson) could potentially threaten the stability of the universe.

A deterministic system cannot exist without predetermined parameters and specifications. 

Take an electronic calculator, for instance. Before it is produced, specifications regarding its display digits, accuracy, and capabilities are established.

Our universe operates as a deterministic system governed by natural laws. 
Thus, it required predefined characteristics regarding these laws, their potential states, and behaviors before our universe came into existence. 

This outcome can only be attributed to a designer.

Consequently, we can assert with absolute confidence that such a source is essential for the existence of our universe, grounded firmly in logical reasoning and rational evidence.

It is crucial to recognize that this source must be, absolutely infinite; it must encompass all existing information and knowledge, and it must possess the capacity to bring things into existence spontaneously, without direct interaction. 
Furthermore, this source cannot embody, any attributes that contradict these essential qualities.

Since our universe had a beginning, we can confidently conclude that-

'A' is the source or entity responsible for its creation. Based on the logical principles we have established, 

'A' must possess certain attributes, and it cannot possess any that contradict these essential qualities.

Firstly, 'A' cannot have a beginning or an end; it must have always existed. Furthermore, 'A' cannot be part of our universe, as that would imply it has a history, and thus, a beginning.

Secondly, 'A' is capable of bringing things into existence from nothing. This quality is essential to ensure that 'A' remains independent of the universe and is not a part of it.

Thirdly, 'A' possesses intelligence, encapsulating all knowledge and information present in our universe.

This brings us directly to Allah (swt). In Islam, 
Allah is the only God that embodies the necessary attributes, abilities, and capabilities outlined above, without any characteristics that contradict these fundamental qualities.

It is imperative to understand that 'A' is eternally existing. 
In the same way, Allah is also eternally existing. The Noble Quran declares:

"Say: He is Allah, the One and Only;
Allah, the Eternal, Absolute;
He begetteth not, nor is He begotten;
And there is none like unto Him."
(Chapter 112)

Allah does not possess size, form, or shape as we comprehend them, because nothing exists that can be compared to Allah.

How do we truly know Allah? We discern Allah's nature through His attributes. Allah (swt) has at least 99 names or attributes, some of which are particularly significant:

Allah is known as 'al-Bâqî', emphasizing the One whose existence has neither beginning nor end, transcending the confines of time.

Moreover, 
'A' embodies all intellect found in our universe, and Allah is all-knowing. He is referred to as 'al-'Alîm', meaning the One who is intuitively aware of all things, even before they happen. 
Nothing is concealed from Him; He possesses complete knowledge of all matters.

'A' brings things into existence from nothing, and Allah creates spontaneously. The Quran states:

"Creator of the heavens and the earth from nothingness; He has only to say, when He wills a thing, 'Be', and it is." (Quran 2:117)

"Verily, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be' – and it is!" (Noble Quran 36:82)

Our universe operates in a deterministic manner, 
aligning seamlessly with the Islamic perspective. As clearly stated, 
"Verily, all things have We created in proportion and measure." (Al-Qur'an 54:49)

It is clear that 'A' is the only rational and logical entity capable of creating our universe. Therefore, 'A' fittingly represents Allah.

So, acknowledge this truth: 'A' unequivocally stands for Allah.

The claim about the existence of Allah is made in the Quran and the burden of proof lies with the one who makes the claim.

So what evidence is there for the Quran itself?

Let's analyse the Noble Quran. 

The Noble Quran is the only Holy Scripture that was interactive.

It was revealed over a period of 23 years, piece by piece. 
Most of the verses serve as responses to specific queries or situations.

For example, when some Jews asked Prophet Muhammad (SAW) to describe God, the following verses were revealed in response:

Surah Al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112):

"Say, 'He is Allah, [who is] One,
Allah, the Eternal Refuge.
He neither begets nor is born,
Nor is there to Him any equivalent.'"

Another example involves the incident with Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, a blind companion of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW). 

When the Prophet was speaking with the leaders of the Quraysh about Islam, Ibn Umm Maktum approached seeking guidance. 

However, the Prophet, prioritizing the leaders, frowned and turned away. As a consequence, verses were revealed that gently reprimanded the Prophet, emphasizing that sincere seekers of truth, regardless of their status, deserve attention.

This illustrates the interactive nature of the revelation.

Another unique aspect of the Quran is that is recital. 
When verses were revealed, 

Prophet Muhammad (SAW) learned them by rote and also taught his companions to memorize them. 
Some of them wrote down the verses to aid their memorization. 

This method of revelation is remarkable because it leaves no room for mistakes. 

If people learned the verses by heart and committed them to memory, any corrections to the revelation would require informing everyone and having them memorize the corrected version, which would become increasingly difficult over time. 

The Quran contains many stories and incidents that are often repeated, making it impractical for Prophet Muhammad (SAW) to keep track of all the minute details spanning over decades, especially considering that he could neither read nor write, like many individuals of that time.

There are many Unique aspect to the Noble Quran that makes it stand out from among other Holy scriptures.

The claim of Divine Origin:

The Quran explicitly claims to be the literal word of God (Allah) as revealed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through the Angel Jibreel (Gabriel). 
Unlike many other scriptures that are viewed as inspired by God.

Preservation of Text:

The Quran has remained unchanged since its revelation over 1,400 years ago. It was meticulously memorized, written down, and compiled during the lifetime of the Prophet and shortly thereafter. Modern manuscripts are identical to the earliest known copies, fulfilling the Quran's own promise that God would protect it from corruption (Surah Al-Hijr 15:9).

Preservation through Mathematical Integrity:

The Quran asserts its preservation in Surah Al-Hijr (15:9): 
"Indeed, it is We who sent down the Quran, and indeed, We will be its guardian." 

Any alteration to the text, even by a single word or letter, disrupts these intricate patterns:

The Quran exhibits balanced occurrences of words that are thematically related:

•The word "Day" (يوم) appears 365 times, corresponding to the number of days in a year.

•The word "Month" (شهر) appears 12 times, matching the number of months in a year.

•Words like "Man" (رجل) and "Woman" (امرأة) each appear 24 times, symbolizing equality in creation.

The number 19 is considered significant in Quranic studies due to its mention in Surah Al-Muddathir (74:30): 
"Over it are nineteen [angels]." Mathematicians and researchers have found many patterns linked to this number:

•The total number of chapters (surahs) in the Quran is 114, which is divisible by 19 (114 = 19 × 6).

•The total number of verses in the Quran is 6,236 (excluding the Basmala at the start of chapters), and its sum of digits (6 + 2 + 3 + 6) is 19.

•The word "Allah" (الله) appears in the Quran 2,698 times, a number also divisible by 19 (2,698 = 19 × 142).

The Basmala (بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ), 
which begins 113 chapters, has unique mathematical properties:

•It consists of 19 letters.

•The frequency of its words in the Quran corresponds to multiples of 19: 

 The word "Ism" (Name) appears 19 times.

The word "Allah" appears 2,698 times, as noted above.

The word "Rahman" (Most Gracious) appears 57 times (57 = 19 × 3).

The word "Raheem" (Most Merciful) appears 114 times (114 = 19 × 6).

Verse Count and Chapter Relations

•The Quran's chapters vary in length, yet their arrangement forms a mathematical relationship. 

For instance: 

The first revealed verse, 96:1 ("Read in the name of your Lord"), 
lies within Surah Al-'Alaq, which is the 19th surah from the end.
These are only a few examples out of many such examples.

Quran's scientific claims before their discovery:

The Noble Quran revealed over 1,400 years ago, contains verses that align with modern scientific knowledge, many of which predate their discovery by centuries.

Embryology

Quranic Verse:

"We created man from a drop of fluid, then placed it in a firm resting place. 
Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into a lump, and 
We made the lump into bones, and We clothed the bones with flesh; then 
We developed him into another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators."
(Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:13-14)

Scientific Context:

This verse describes the stages of embryonic development with remarkable precision:

•The "drop of fluid" (nutfa) refers to sperm and egg.

•The "clinging clot" (alaqah) corresponds to the embryo attaching to the uterine wall.

•The "lump" (mudghah) is an early stage of the fetus.

•The development of bones and flesh aligns with modern embryology. This process was not scientifically detailed until the invention of microscopes in the 17th century.

"And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander."
(Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:47)

Scientific Context:

This verse suggests the concept of an expanding universe, 
which was confirmed by Edwin Hubble in 1929 through redshift observations. 
Before this discovery, the prevailing belief was that the universe was static and unchanging.

The Quranic phrase  "We are [its] expander" 
In Surah Adh-Dhariyat 51:47 uses language that implies continuous action, 
suggesting that the universe is still expanding. 
This aligns strikingly with modern cosmology.

"Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?"
(Surah Al-Anbiya 21:30)

Scientific Context:

The verse from Surah Al-Anbiya 21:30 aligns intriguingly with modern cosmological theories, particularly the Big Bang Theory and its stages, including the singularity and the inflation stage.

"And made from water every living thing"

1. Origin of Life and Water:

•The emphasis on water as the origin of life aligns with modern biology, which confirms that water is essential for the survival and development of all known life forms.

•Early Earth theories suggest that water played a crucial role in the emergence of life, and it remains fundamental to the biochemistry of living organisms.

These insights, revealed over 1,400 years ago, correspond to concepts that were only scientifically articulated in the 20th century.

"Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses—We will drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise."
(Surah An-Nisa 4:56)

Scientific Context:

Modern science has discovered that pain receptors are located in the skin, not deeper tissues. This was unknown in the 7th century.

Hence,

If a word were added or removed, the balanced counts of thematic words would no longer hold.
Changing a single letter in the Basmala would disrupt its 19-letter structure.
Altering the arrangement or content of chapters would break the numerical relationships tied to the number 19 or chapter symmetry.

Prophet Muhammad (saw) himself lead a very active and busy life, 
He was an administrator and ruler, 
He fought the war, and people constantly came to him for advice, 
He was also an Imam who led people 5 times a day in prayers and during the night he prayed for long hours,
He had multiple wives to take care.

It would be impossible for Prophet Muhammad to have produced such a remarkable and unparalleled scripture.

Considering the above facts and insights and given that the Quran shows no clear contradictions or discrepancies in its verses, the scientific information before scientific discovery and the mathematical relation between the verses and the fact it was an interactive revelation conveyed over 23 years are remarkably consistent, it is clear that the Quran could not have been produced by Prophet Muhammad (SAW).

The Quran itself points out in 4:82: 

"Will they not then ponder on the Quran? If it had been from other than Allah, they would have found therein much incongruity."

Considering all of this, it becomes evident that the 
Quran is not the work of Prophet Muhammad (SAW).

But why no clear-cut and absolute evidence for the existence of God?

Quran answers it!

Surah Al-Mulk (67:2):
"[He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed – and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving."

This verse explicitly mentions that life and death were created to test human beings in their actions and character.

Surah Ash-Shams (91:7-10):
"And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it and inspired it with discernment of its wickedness and its righteousness, He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who instills it [with corruption]."

Here, humans are shown to have the ability to recognize good and evil and are responsible for their own moral choices.

We have been given free will to make choices in the world and our success in the next life depends upon it.

The Noble Quran makes this very clear.

"This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for those conscious of Allah - Who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them."
(Al-Baqarah 2:2-3)

So having clear-cut absolute evidence does not make logical and rational sense because it will defeat the very purpose the Noble Quran says we are living this worldly life.

"And declare, “The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to vanish.”  (Al Quran 17:81)
